'''Jacqueline Ferrand''' (17 February 1918 &ndash; 26 April 2014) was a French mathematician who worked on [[conformal map|conformal]] [[representation theory]], [[potential theory]], and [[Riemannian manifold]]s. She taught at universities in Caen, Lille, and Paris.<ref>[https://www.math.u-psud.fr/~pansu/ferrand.html Curriculum vitae]; accessed 5 May 2014.</ref><ref>[https://smf.emath.fr/content/décès-de-jacqueline-ferrand Jacqueline Ferrand profile], smf.emath.fr; accessed 5 May 2014 {{in lang|fr}}</ref><ref>[https://www.math.u-psud.fr/~pansu/ferrand.html Lelong-Ferrand profile]; accessed 5 May 2014. {{in lang|fr}}</ref> 

== Early life and education ==

Marie Odile Jacqueline Ferrand was born in [[Alès]], in southern France. The daughter of a classics teacher, she attended the [[lycée]] in [[Nîmes]].<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Ferrand}}</ref> Excelling in mathematics, she won the first prize in a national mathematics competition while there.<ref name=lr>{{cite web|url=https://mathwomen.agnesscott.org/women/ferrand.htm|title=Jacqueline Ferrand|author=Riddle, Lars|publisher=Biographies of Women Mathematicians, Agnes Scott College|date=19 February 2025|access-date=30 June 2026}}</ref>

In 1936 the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris began admitting women, and she was one of the first to apply and be admitted to study mathematics and science. In 1939 she and [[Roger Apéry]] placed first in the mathematics [[agrégation]].<ref name=lr/>

== Career ==
She began teaching at the [[École normale supérieure de jeunes filles]], an elite teacher training college for girls in [[Sèvres]], while continuing to do mathematics research under the supervision of [[Arnaud Denjoy]].<ref name=lr/> She published three papers in 1941 and defended a doctoral thesis in 1942.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name=lr/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=188260}}</ref>

In June 1942, in connection with her doctorate (doctorat-es-sciences), she published two papers: "Étude de la correspondence entre les frontières dans la représentation conforme" and "Étude de la représentation conforme au voisinage de la frontière".<ref name=lr/> As a result, in 1943 she won the Girbal-Baral Prize of the [[French Academy of Sciences]], and obtained a faculty position at the [[University of Bordeaux]]. She moved to the [[University of Caen]] in 1945 and was given a chair at the [[University of Lille]] in 1948, which she held until 1956. After a sabbatical at [[Princeton University]], she was then appointed a profession at the [[University of Paris]], becoming one of the first female full professors in the science faculty.<ref name=lr/> She retired in 1984.<ref name="mactutor" /><ref name=lr/><ref name="yks">{{citation|title=Women mathematicians in France in the mid-twentieth century|first=Yvette|last=Kosmann-Schwarzbach|doi=10.1080/17498430.2014.976804|journal=BSHM Bulletin: Journal of the British Society for the History of Mathematics|volume=30|issue=3|pages=227–242|year=2015|arxiv=1502.07597|bibcode=2015arXiv150207597K|s2cid=119148294}}.</ref>

==Contributions==
Ferrand undertook research in the areas of analysis and geometry, especially [[Conformal map|conformal representation]] (from 1942), [[potential theory]] (from 1947), and from 1955 [[Riemannian manifold|Riemann manifolds]] and [[Hodge theory|harmonic forms]].<ref name=lr/><ref name=ek>{{cite book |last=Kramer |first=Edna |date=1970 |title=The Nature and Growth of Modern Mathematics |publisher=Hawthorn Books, Inc. |location=New York |isbn=978-0691023724 |page=709.711}}</ref>

The thesis she defended in 1942, as well as later papers, addressed [[Conformal geometry|conformal transformations]] in relation to a neighbouring [[Boundary (topology)|boundary point]]. In subsequent papers, she developed a concept she called "preholomorphic functions" as the basis of a new methodology for [[mathematical proof]]s.<ref name=ek/><ref name=pp/>

Researching [[potential theory]], she was able to undertake work on theorems such as the lemmas of [[Julia Wolf]] and [[Phragmén–Lindelöf principle|Phragmén-Lindelöf]] by generalising them to ''n'' dimensions. She went on to tackle the field's most difficult problems, once again on the basis of the new concepts she created.<ref name=ek/>

From 1958 to 1968, Ferrand was less active in the research field, devoting most of her time to raising her four children. She nevertheless prepared a number of university courses. Initially simply duplicated, as a result of their popularity they were later published as books. They included a course on differential geometry, published by Masson in 1983, as well as undergraduate courses published by [[Armand Colin]] (1964) and Dunod (1967).<ref name=pp/>  

In 1955, she turned from research to writing, producing a comprehensive treatise titled "Représentation conforme et transformations à intégrale de Dirichlet bornée" published in the Collections de Cahiers Scientifiques.<ref name=ek/>

Ferrand had nearly 100 mathematical publications, including ten books,<ref name=lr/> and was active in mathematical research into her late 70s.<ref name="mactutor"/> One of her accomplishments, in 1971, was to prove the [[compact group|compactness]] of the group of conformal mappings of a non-spherical compact [[Riemannian manifold]], resolving a conjecture of [[André Lichnerowicz]], and on the basis of this work she became an invited speaker at the 1974 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Vancouver]].<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="yks"/>

While Ferrand's work has significantly influenced various areas of mathematics, her research has not been widely recognised in France. As a result of international collaboration, she has nevertheless been appreciated abroad, especially in Finland where her work has enjoyed considerable interest.<ref name=pp/>

==Personal life==
Ferrand married mathematician [[Pierre Lelong]] in 1947, taking his surname alongside hers in her subsequent publications<ref name=lr/> until their separation in 1977.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="yks"/> They had four children, born in 1949, 1951, 1952 and 1958.<ref name=lr/><ref name=pp>{{cite web|url=https://www.imo.universite-paris-saclay.fr/~pierre.pansu/ferrand.html|title=Jacqueline Ferrand et son oeuvre|author=Pansu, P.|publisher=Université Paris Saclay|date=11 April 1997|access-date=1 July 2026|language=French}}</ref>

Ferrand died at her home on 26 April 2014 age 96.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FERRAND Jacqueline - 1936 s {{!}} a-Ulm |url=https://www.archicubes.ens.fr/lassociation/m%C3%A9moire-normalienne/notices/ferrand-jacqueline-1936-s |access-date=2026-07-29 |website=www.archicubes.ens.fr}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
In 2026, Jacqueline Ferrand was announced as one of 72 historical women in STEM whose names have been proposed to be added to the [[List of the 72 names on the Eiffel Tower|72 men]] already celebrated on the [[Eiffel Tower]]. The idea was conceived by a student and tour guide named Bernard Rigaud and then championed by [[Nathalie Drach-Temam]], the President of Sorbonne University.<ref name=hypat>{{Cite web |title=The Hypatia project: engraving the names of 72 women scientists on the Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en}}</ref> The plan was announced by the Mayor of Paris, [[Anne Hidalgo]] following the recommendations of a committee led by [[Isabelle Vauglin]] of [[Femmes et Sciences]] and Jean-François Martins, representing the operating company which runs the Eiffel Tower.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Eiffel Tower: a list of 72 women scientists will soon be inscribed on the Parisian monument |url=https://www.sortiraparis.com/en/news/in-paris/articles/340564-eiffel-tower-list-of-72-women-scientists-soon-to-be-honored-on-the-paris-landmark |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=www.sortiraparis.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2026-01-26 |title=Eiffel Tower to honor 72 women scientists for posterity |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/france/article/2026/01/26/eiffel-tower-to-honor-72-women-in-science-for-posterity_6749828_7.html |access-date=2026-02-05 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Les noms des 72 femmes pour la Tour Eiffel ont été révélés. |url=https://www.femmesetsciences.fr/news/les-noms-des-72-femmes-pour-la-tour-eiffel-ont-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-r%C3%A9v%C3%A9l%C3%A9 |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Femmes & Sciences |language=fr}}</ref><ref>[https://10ca8303-b3dc-4a91-9dcc-2d2b91792b47.usrfiles.com/ugd/10ca83_3838bd19a41a4e83927cfc8fe0f50404.pdf 72 femmes de sciences pour la tour Eiffel] ''Femmes & Sciences'' (in French). Retrieved 2026-03-23</ref>
